newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: YACHTING-TEAM NZ SHOW CLASS IN MINI AMERICA'S CUP.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-TEAM NZ SHOW CLASS IN MINI AMERICA'S CUP.

text.p: Team New Zealand showed why they are the holders of yachting's most prized trophy when they sank The Royal Dorset Yacht Club four races to one in the final of the mini America's Cup regatta on Auckland's Waitemata Harbour on Sunday.

In near-perfect conditions with a 15-knot breeze, the New Zealand boat Black Magic comprehensively outsailed its British rival, winning three races in succession to take the best-of-seven final after both teams had won a race each on Saturday.

The British, who have not sailed in the America's Cup for a decade, reached the final on Saturday morning after heading off the three other challengers -- from New York, San Francisco and France -- in a series of races held over the past week.

Team New Zealand skipper Russell Coutts said the sailing had been a lot closer than the final result suggested and much had been gained from the regatta, held as a warm-up for the real event which starts in late 1999.
"It showed that in smooth water out in the gulf there's going to be bloody close racing in 1999-2000," he said.
